name: Koguryo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct; attested only via Chinese-transcribed toponym glosses (Beckwith 2004, Vovin 2005 are comparative); no stress description possible or found.

sources.citation: 板橋義三 (Itabashi Yoshizō). 2004. 高句麗の地名から高句麗語と朝鮮語・日本語との史的関係をさぐる. In A. Vovin & T. Osada (eds.), 日本語系統論の現在 (Nichibunken Sōsho 31), 131-185. Kyoto: International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
sources.note: §3.3 音韻的特徴 ('phonological features', p. ~150) lists segmental/structural traits only (e.g. (1) lack of word-final vowels, CVC roots vs Japanese CVCV); no occurrence of アクセント, 声調, 高低, ピッチ or 'accent/tone/stress' anywhere in the 55-page text.
No phonology or prosody section; states the evidence is 'extremely sparse' (numerals and a few glossed toponyms).

sources.citation: 李丞宰 (Lee Seungjae). 2020. 古代漢字音の音韻対立研究方法論 — 高句麗語、百濟語、中国前期中古漢語を中心に. AJKL 16: 139-191.
sources.note: Open PDF already saved but image-only; needs Japanese scanned (tesseract jpn data not installed here) to check whether tone of the phonograms is discussed.

sources.citation: Pellard, Thomas. 2005. Review of Beckwith (2004) Koguryo, the Language of Japan's Continental Relatives. Korean Studies 29: 167-170. doi:10.1353/ks.2006.0008 (open HAL draft hal-00194111).
sources.note: Nothing on accent/tone/stress. Describes Beckwith's reconstruction of 'the phonological system of his OKog, as well as 139 Koguryo words' from Samguk sagi toponyms and notes the source language of the place names is uncertain ('pseudo-Koguryo').

sources.citation: 馬淵和夫・李寅泳・大橋康子 (Mabuchi Kazuo, Lee In-yeong & Ohashi Yasuko). 1980. 『三国史記』記載の「高句麗」地名より見た古代高句麗語の考察. 文藝言語研究 言語篇 (University of Tsukuba) 5. hdl:2241/13518.
sources.note: 第三章 音韻組織 (ch. 3 'phonological system') reconstructs vowel (1. 母音組織) and consonant (2. 子音組織) inventories from the Chinese transcription characters; nothing on accent, tone or stress (only one mention of the Chinese entering-tone 入声 of a character).

sources.citation: Nam Pung-hyun. 2012. Old Korean. In N. Tranter (ed.), The Languages of Japan and Korea, 41-72. Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Handbook chapter covering the Three Kingdoms languages including Koguryo; would supersede nothing but could confirm the absence of prosodic data.

sources.note: Google Books GData snippets only (book paywalled). Index of the 2004 ed.: 'pitch accent, 22, 26, 33, 160; see also tones'. Body snippet (both eds., same paragraph, page not shown): '..monosyllabicity, pitch accents, and verb-final syntax (there is no information available on pitch accents in Koguryo, but the other features do apply to it as well and it is probable that Common Japanese-Koguryoic may be characterized in the same way)'. Also p. 11: Japanese described as 'a heavily monosyllabic pitch accent language (Sakakura 1993; Kiyose 1997, 2001: 135)'. 'Tone' hits concern Middle Chinese tone…
